ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\text{Rt}\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, points $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Extend $BC$ to point $F$ such that $CF=\frac{1}{2}BC$. If $AB=10$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that points D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC, respectively,

$\therefore$ $AD=BD=\frac{1}{2}AB=5$, DE is the midline of $\triangle ACB$, AE=CE

$\therefore$ $DE\parallel BC$, $DE=\frac{1}{2}BC$,

$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CF=\frac{1}{2}BC$,

$\therefore$ $\angle DEA=\angle FCE=90^\circ$, CF=ED,

$\therefore$ $\triangle AED\cong \triangle ECF$ (SAS),

$\therefore$ EF=AD=\boxed{5}.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is right triangle ABC, AC is drawn as a horizontal line, BC is drawn as a vertical line, and there is a right-angle mark at C; point F is on the extension line of BC passing through C downward; point E is on AC, point D is on AB, and the vertical DE and the oblique line EF are drawn. The problem gives that D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC, and CF=1/2 BC, AB=10.

Reasoning: Because D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC in triangle ABC, DE is the midline of triangle ABC, so DE ∥ BC, and DE=1/2 BC. Also because CF=1/2 BC, DE=CF. Since ∠ACB=90°, AC ⟂ BC; and DE ∥ BC, so DE ⟂ AC, therefore ∠DEA=90°. At the same time, CF is on the extension line of BC, and CE is on AC, so ∠FCE=90°. Also because E is the midpoint of AC, AE=CE. Thus AE=CE, DE=CF, and the included angles ∠DEA=∠FCE=90°, so △AED ≅ △ECF (SAS). Therefore the corresponding side EF=AD. D is the midpoint of AB, AB=10, so AD=10/2=5, hence EF=5.
